newsitem.title: ZAIRE: U.N. evacuates some staff from Kinshasa - source.
newsitem.headline: U.N. evacuates some staff from Kinshasa - source.

text.p: United Nations agencies stepped up security precaution in the rebel-targeted Zairean capital on Tuesday, evacuating a handful of non-essential staff, a senior U.N. source said.
"We are sending away non-essential staff. It will involve the departure of about five people, leaving about 15 people in Kinshasa," the source told Reuters.
Laurent Kabila's rebels are closing in on Kinshasa and more than 3,000 American, Belgian, French and British troops are stationed in Central Africa ready to evacuate foreigners.

The U.N. source said those remaining were heads of United Nations agencies and a few key staff. Tuesday's decision became automatic when the United Nations raised its security level to phase four. The highest level -- phase five -- is complete evacuation, he said.
Asked why the move became necessary, the source said: "In the U.N. the more they (rebels) approach the more we have a tendency to leave as a precaution."
